name: Guardian genius crossword No 202
preamble: Fill in the blanks with a word (or, in two cases, a two-word phrase) that enables you to solve the clue. The words inserted are all also solutions to clues.

solutions.check: grid and clues read from the Guardian's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Swiss ____ taking census regularly without grounds

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the word that follows, at even steps

blocks.note: the blank is CITY (12 across); Basel is a Swiss city
the second, fourth and sixth letters of census

explanation.surface: A Swiss town counting its people every so often, for no good reason.
explanation.walkthrough: Fill the blank with CITY from 12 across: a Swiss city is BASEL, which then takes on ESS to make BASELESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Something baseless has no foundation, which is the same idea as being without grounds.

clue.text: Arm supporter with ____ Nordic bomb?

indicators.note: the blank is DRAINED (16 across): a drained word is emptied of its middle, leaving its outer letters

blocks.note: a bra is an item of supporting underwear
the first and last letters of Nordic
H as in H-bomb, the hydrogen bomb

explanation.surface: A weapons-supporter armed with an exhausted Scandinavian bomb.
explanation.walkthrough: DRAINED fills the blank, emptying Nordic to NC; the question mark flags bomb as H-bomb.
explanation.definitionFit: A branch is an arm of an organisation or of a tree, an offshoot of the main body.

clue.text: Just a little bit evil to join ____ antics

indicators.note: the blank is CHAOTIC (19 across): something chaotic is in disorder, so the letters are scrambled
to join here means to enter among the others, so one piece goes inside

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
ill can mean evil, as in ill will

explanation.surface: A touch of wickedness joins some wild horseplay.
explanation.walkthrough: The blank takes CHAOTIC from 19 across, which serves as the instruction to scramble the word after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A scintilla is a tiny trace or spark, the smallest amount of something.

clue.text: Revolutionary ____ maintains eastern spring

indicators.note: a revolution is a turning round, so the word is read backwards
maintains means holds, so the turned word keeps another letter inside it

blocks.note: the blank is CHINA (11 across): china plate is rhyming slang for mate, a pal
E is the abbreviation for eastern

explanation.surface: Revolutionary China keeps its eastern hot springs.
explanation.walkthrough: In Cockney rhyming slang, china (china plate) means mate. Turned round, PAL becomes LAP, which holds E.
explanation.definitionFit: To leap is to spring, a jump into the air.

clue.text: ____ lost points over skid

indicators.note: lost suggests the letters have gone astray and must be found in a new order
over means covering, so the rearranged letters lie over and around the other piece

blocks.note: the blank is UNITED (9 down), abbreviated U as in football club names like Man U
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A football side dropped points after a slip.
explanation.walkthrough: UNITED fills the blank and shrinks to U, which sits inside a mix of POINTS.
explanation.definitionFit: A spin-out is a car skidding and spinning off its course.

clue.text: Guardian setters had to ____ assets oddly thrown away

indicators.note: the blank is SEIZE (24 down): to seize something is to grip it, so one piece holds the other
oddly means keeping only the letters in odd-numbered positions of the next word

blocks.note: the setters speak as WE, and had is contracted to 'D, giving WE'D
the first, third and fifth letters of assets

explanation.surface: The crossword setters at a newspaper had to grab assets that had been dumped.
explanation.walkthrough: The blank takes SEIZE from 24 down. Setters writing collectively call themselves we, and had shortens to an apostrophe-d.
explanation.definitionFit: Wasted resources are squandered, and something squandered has been thrown away.

clue.text: Active ____ starts to get overwhelmed by a poorly synced command

indicators.note: starts are beginnings, so each word gives its first letter
to be overwhelmed is to be engulfed, so these pieces end up inside the rest
poorly means badly done, so the letters of the word after it are out of order

blocks.note: A is the grammatical abbreviation for active
taken as written, to be rearranged
taken as written
the blank is NERVE CELL (17 down); the starts of its two words

explanation.surface: An active brain cell swamped by a badly timed order.
explanation.walkthrough: NERVE CELL from 17 down fills the blank; it is the two-word phrase whose initials are wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: Ascendancy is dominance or control over others, which is having command.

clue.text: Object to judge's ____ dogma, essentially

indicators.note: the blank is BASELESS (1 across): in a down clue the base is the last letter, so it is removed
essentially means at its heart, so the central letter of the word is used

blocks.note: to judge something is to think it, as in to deem
the middle letter of dogma

explanation.surface: Raising an objection to a judge's unfounded doctrine.
explanation.walkthrough: Object looks like a verb here but is the noun. BASELESS fills the blank, so THINK loses its bottom letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A thing is an object, any item that can be named.

clue.text: Servant's in the ____ on the inside of BDSM suit

indicators.note: the blank is ASCENDANCY (6 down): ascending in a down clue means going upwards, so the word is read bottom to top
the inside of a word is its middle, leaving out the outer letters

blocks.note: a maid is a female servant
taken as written
the two inner letters of BDSM

explanation.surface: A servant gets the upper hand within a bondage outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: With ASCENDANCY in the blank, MAID climbs upwards and reads DIAM. Suit is not clothing but a suit of cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Diamonds is one of the four suits in a pack of playing cards.

clue.text: As one has solver given courtly title, ____

indicators.note: the blank is VERBALLY (30 across): something said verbally is spoken, so the words are judged by sound

blocks.note: the solver is you, and a courtly title like Sir is given by being knighted

explanation.surface: The puzzle solver being given a knighthood, put into words.
explanation.walkthrough: VERBALLY fills the blank; YOU KNIGHTED, said out, gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting as one means acting together in agreement, being united.

clue.text: Movement in which an atom ____ iodine mass

indicators.note: the blank is ECLIPSES (18 down): to eclipse is to block out by covering, so one piece surrounds another

blocks.note: taken as written
an ion is an atom carrying an electric charge
I is the chemical symbol for iodine
a mat can be a thick tangled mass, as of hair

explanation.surface: A chemistry scene: an atom outshining an iodine mass, set in motion.
explanation.walkthrough: ECLIPSES from 18 down fills the blank. Strictly an ion is a charged atom rather than any atom, a looseness the blog's commenters noted.
explanation.definitionFit: Animation is liveliness or the act of bringing to life, a state of motion and activity.

clue.text: Material from ____ in Amazon

indicators.note: from says the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows, not whole words

blocks.note: the blank is BRANCH (1 down); its last two letters
taken as written
the opening letter of Amazon

explanation.surface: Some substance obtained from a part of the Amazon rainforest.
explanation.walkthrough: Put BRANCH from 1 down in the blank and the answer is hidden across it, in and Amazon; it is shown as pieces only because the checker cannot see into the blank.
explanation.definitionFit: China is porcelain, a ceramic material used for crockery.

clue.text: Metropolis is about ____ ghost story, ultimately

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so each word gives only its final letter

blocks.note: c is short for circa, Latin for about
the blank is SCI-FI (27 across); the last letters of sci-fi, ghost and story

explanation.surface: Metropolis, the old film, described as a science-fiction ghost tale.
explanation.walkthrough: With SCI-FI in the blank, C for about leads the final letters I, T and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: A metropolis is a large and important city.

clue.text: Love for one ____ bursting green round the country

indicators.note: X for Y means one letter takes the place of another in the word
bursting suggests the letters are blown apart and scattered into a new order

blocks.note: love is zero in tennis scoring, shaped like the letter O
one is I as a Roman numeral; this letter is the one replaced
the blank is HERB (26 down), and mint is a herb
taken as written
a round shape is the letter O

explanation.surface: Swapping a herb for love as green bursts all around the land.
explanation.walkthrough: HERB from 26 down fills the blank, and the herb needed is a common garden one; round then adds a ring-shaped letter to the scrambled colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Montenegro is a small Balkan nation on the Adriatic coast.

clue.text: Having gin and tonic to forget about day and get ____

indicators.note: forgetting about something leaves it out, so a letter is removed
the blank is WASTED (5 across): being wasted is being drunk, so the letters stagger into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
D is the abbreviation for day; this is the letter dropped

explanation.surface: Drinking gin and tonics, ignoring the time of day, and getting drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: WASTED fills the blank and is British slang for very drunk; the cocktail loses D, then the rest is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Containing means including or holding, which is having something within.

clue.text: Close to a large street on the outskirts of ____

indicators.note: pieces on the outskirts sit around the outside of something else, enclosing it

blocks.note: taken as written
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
St is the address abbreviation for street
the blank is MONTENEGRO (13 across); its outskirts are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Directions: near a big road on the edge of a Balkan country.
explanation.walkthrough: MONTENEGRO from 13 across fills the blank. Outskirts does double duty, trimming that country to its edges and placing the other pieces around them.
explanation.definitionFit: Close to used of a number or amount means nearly, so it can stand in for almost.

clue.text: Spent ____ fell from the sky

blocks.note: the blank is DIAMONDS (8 down), the card suit abbreviated to D
rain is water falling from the sky

explanation.surface: Used-up diamonds dropped out of the sky.
explanation.walkthrough: DIAMONDS fills the blank, and in bridge notation diamonds is D.
explanation.definitionFit: Drained and spent both mean exhausted, with nothing left.

clue.text: ____ students supporting spirit's corporeal messenger?

indicators.note: in a down clue a supporting piece sits below, so it comes after what it holds up

blocks.note: nerve and spirit both mean courage
the blank is CHURCH (20 down), abbreviated CE for the Church of England
L is a learner or student, as on a learner driver's L-plate, so two of them

explanation.surface: Church students as the bodily messengers of the spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: CHURCH fills the blank. The order is set by supporting: the church and students sit under spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: A nerve cell is a neuron, carrying signals around the body, so it is a messenger in the flesh.

clue.text: Astronomical events are less epic in ____

indicators.note: the blank is ANIMATION (10 across): letters in animation are set in motion and move about

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Space spectacles seem smaller when shown as cartoons.
explanation.walkthrough: ANIMATION fills the blank and tells you to set those two words in motion.
explanation.definitionFit: Eclipses happen when one heavenly body blocks the light of another, events studied in astronomy.

clue.text: American books ____ clothing all over the shop

indicators.note: clothing means dressing around, so one piece wraps around the others

blocks.note: the blank is TRENDY (22 down), and chic means trendy
A is a standard abbreviation for American
OT is the Old Testament, a collection of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Fashionable American books wrapping clothes scattered everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: TRENDY from 22 down fills the blank; books is the usual crossword shorthand for one of the two Testaments.
explanation.definitionFit: All over the shop is a British idiom for disorganised, which is what chaotic means.

clue.text: Short friend and Roman Catholic jump on end of ____ to reach temple

indicators.note: short means cut off, so the word loses its final letter
the end of a word is its last letter

blocks.note: a chum is a friend
RC is the abbreviation for Roman Catholic
the blank is SLEIGH (29 across); its final letter

explanation.surface: A short friend and a Catholic hop on the back of a sleigh to get to the temple.
explanation.walkthrough: SLEIGH from 29 across fills the blank; jump on just places the pieces one after another.
explanation.definitionFit: A church is a building for worship, and temple is a general word for one.

clue.text: Rejecting premieres, star resents agent churning ____ for awards

indicators.note: premieres are first showings, so the first letter of each word is taken
rejecting means throwing back, so the collected letters are read in the opposite order

blocks.note: the blank is SPIN-OUT (4 down), read as two words, spin and out

explanation.surface: A film star is annoyed that their agent keeps churning out spin for awards season.
explanation.walkthrough: SPIN-OUT counts as two words, giving both S and O; the six first letters are then read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oscars are the Academy Awards, Hollywood's annual film prizes.

clue.text: Use drug ____ ecstasy, right, when leaving island

indicators.note: the blank is CONTAINING (14 down), so the word before it holds the pieces after it
leaving means departing, so that letter goes out of the word

blocks.note: an opiate is a drug derived from opium
E is slang for the drug ecstasy
R is the abbreviation for right
I is the map abbreviation for island; this letter is removed

explanation.surface: Taking a drug laced with ecstasy, right after leaving the island.
explanation.walkthrough: CONTAINING fills the blank: OPIATE drops its I and holds E and R.
explanation.definitionFit: To operate a machine is to use it, work it or run it.

clue.text: Stylish fan dismissing the ____: too nerdy?

indicators.note: dismissing means sending away, so those letters are taken out
to fan is to spread out, so the letters are spread into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
the blank is OSCARS (21 across); Oscar is O in the NATO alphabet, so two of them

explanation.surface: A film fan who snubs the Academy Awards for being too geeky.
explanation.walkthrough: With OSCARS in the blank, the two Os go from TOO NERDY and the rest is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Trendy means fashionable, following the latest style.

clue.text: Fashionable society ____ recalled by half-hearted trainees in schools

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so this word is read backwards
half-hearted means losing half of the middle, so one of its two central letters goes

blocks.note: in means fashionable
S is a standard abbreviation for society
the blank is THING (7 down), and it can mean a thing
tutees are people being taught by a tutor

explanation.surface: A trendy society thing remembered by trainees who lack enthusiasm at school.
explanation.walkthrough: THING from 7 down fills the blank. Half-hearted is exact: the trainees' word has two letters at its heart and loses one of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Institutes are educational establishments, a formal word for schools or colleges.

clue.text: Apprehend what's left of vacuous cryptic, we ____

indicators.note: vacuous means empty, so the word is emptied of its middle, keeping its ends
the blank is HEAR (25 across): what we hear is a sound, so the letters are said aloud

blocks.note: the outer letters of cryptic are two Cs, said as a plural

explanation.surface: Grasp what remains of an empty crossword clue, we're told.
explanation.walkthrough: HEAR fills the blank. Cryptic emptied is C and C, and two Cs spoken sound like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To apprehend is to arrest or take hold of, which is to seize.

clue.text: Try a ____ of horseradish with some corn?

indicators.note: the blank is SCINTILLA (2 down), a tiny trace, so only one letter, the first, is taken

blocks.note: the opening letter of horseradish
an ear of corn is the seed-bearing head of the plant

explanation.surface: A recipe tip: test a trace of horseradish with a little corn.
explanation.walkthrough: With SCINTILLA in the blank, a scintilla of horseradish is its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To hear a case is to try it in court, as a judge does.

clue.text: Nuclei from lithium converter ____ urban plant

indicators.note: a nucleus is the central core, so the middle letter of each word is used

blocks.note: the blank is OPERATE (21 down); the middle letters of the four words

explanation.surface: A nuclear lab where a lithium converter runs a town power plant.
explanation.walkthrough: OPERATE fills the blank; each of the four words is odd in length and gives its single centre letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A herb is a plant valued for flavour or medicine.

clue.text: Sort of film shown by extremely scholastic ____ around France

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes of the word, its first and last letters
around means the pieces before it enclose the one after it

blocks.note: the first and last letters of scholastic
the blank is INSTITUTES (23 across); I abbreviates institute, so two of them are two Is
F is the international vehicle code for France

explanation.surface: A kind of film screened by academic institutions across France.
explanation.walkthrough: INSTITUTES fills the blank: I is the abbreviation for institute, as in IEE, so the plural is two Is, which go round F.
explanation.definitionFit: Sci-fi is science fiction, a genre of film as well as of books.

clue.text: ____ whose surroundings could be virtually cloned — ha!

indicators.note: virtually means almost, so the word loses its final letter
could be says the letters might be rearranged into something else
surroundings are what lies around, so these letters enclose the setter's own pronoun

blocks.note: taken as written, before its last letter is dropped
taken as written
the blank is the setter's own pseudonym, so the one with these surroundings is the setter, who is me

explanation.surface: A lizard so good at blending in that its background looks copied, and the setter laughs.
explanation.walkthrough: The blank is this very answer, which is also the setter's pseudonym, so the setter's own pronoun sits inside the mixed letters. The setter confirmed this on the blog.
explanation.definitionFit: The blank holds the lizard's name, which is also this setter's pseudonym, so it defines itself.

clue.text: Vehicle leads to Santa leaving with ____ all the reindeer, traditionally

indicators.note: the leads of words are their opening letters, so the start of each is kept
the blank is ALMOST (15 across): almost all of a word means its last letter is dropped

blocks.note: the first letters of Santa and leaving
Santa traditionally has eight reindeer, before Rudolph was added

explanation.surface: Father Christmas setting off with nearly all his reindeer in his vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: ALMOST fills the blank, so EIGHT, the traditional number of Santa's reindeer, loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleigh is a sledge drawn by animals, a vehicle for snow.

clue.text: Labour minister backed the introduction of ____ years in speech

indicators.note: backed means put into reverse, so the two words before it are read backwards
the introduction of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: Lab is the abbreviation for the UK Labour Party
a minister of religion is styled the Rev, short for Reverend
the blank is LEAP (3 down); its opening letter
Y is a standard abbreviation for years

explanation.surface: A Labour politician supported introducing leap years, in a speech.
explanation.walkthrough: Labour is the UK's main centre-left party. LEAP fills the blank, and LAB REV read backwards is VERBAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something verbally means putting it into spoken words, that is, in speech.
